title: Social Influence: Conformity, Compliance, Obedience
summary: Social influence: conformity (Asch), compliance techniques and obedience (Milgram). Covers mechanisms, factors affecting influence and classic experiments.
objectives: Compare the three types of social influence.
revision: Social influence: conformity (Asch), compliance and obedience (Milgram), compared with mechanisms and classic experiments.

notes.t: Changing one's behaviour or beliefs to match those of a group, due to real or imagined group pressure.
Asch's conformity experiments demonstrated that participants conformed to obviously incorrect majority judgments, showing the power of normative social influence.
Agreeing to a request or demand from another person or group, often due to social pressure or persuasion techniques.
Following direct orders from an authority figure, even when the orders conflict with personal conscience.
Milgram's obedience experiments showed that ordinary people would administer apparently painful electric shocks when instructed by an authority figure, revealing the power of legitimate authority.
UGC NET frequently asks about Asch's conformity findings and Milgram's obedience study, including factors that increase or decrease obedience.

mnemonics.title: CCO
mnemonics.text: C — Conformity (group pressure, Asch), C — Compliance (request, foot-in-door), O — Obedience (authority, Milgram)

flashcards.a: Agreeing to a request from another person.
